full_judgment:
2. Short facts for disposal of the Rule are that the decree holder opposite parties as plaintiffs filed. Original Suit No. 20 of 2017 (Title Suit No.29 of 2000/Money Suit No. 5 of 2015) in the Court of the learned District Judge, 14 Cum Commercial Court, Dhanbad, India against Rupali Bank Limited and Rural Electrification Board (REB), Dhaka, Bangladesh for recovery of L/C payment. Ultimately, the said suit was decreed on contest by judgment and decree dated 1-9-2018. 

 3. In this backdrop, the decree holder Anvil Investment Private Ltd. and others to execute the decree as applicants filed Money Execution Case No. 4 of 2023 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Dhaka. 

 4. Thereafter, while the execution case was in progress, on 17-4-2024 the decree-holder opposite parties filed an application under Order XXXVIII, rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure for attachment of bank accounts. The learned District Judge on the same day after hearing the application by the impugned order No. 9 dated 17-4-2024 allowed the application for attachment before judgment. 

 6. Mr. Mohammad Mosfequr Salehin, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in the course of argument takes us through the impugned order, application under Order XXXVIII, rule 5 and other materials on record and then submits that the allegations as attributed in the application for attachment before judgment are untrue, motivated and not tenable in law inasmuch as the decree-holder company without complying the mandatory provisions under Order XXXVIII, rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed the application for attachment before judgment and thus, the order of attachment before Judgment dated 17-4-2024 is misconceived, contrary to provisions under Order XXXVIII, rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure and, as such„ the same is liable to be set-aside. He further submits, it is on record that the decree holder Indian company filed the execution case in order to execute a foreign decree and thereafter, the judgment-debtor bank filed an application under section 44A(3) read with section 13 CPC praying as to maintainability of the execution case but the learned District Judge kept the said application pending for hearing on 9-11-2023 and without disposal of the said application readily allowed the subsequent misconceived application for attachment before judgment in a slipshod manner by the impugned order. Finally, the learned Advocate submits that the impugned order of attachment before judgment was passed beyond the scope of law and, as such„ the same is liable to be set-aside. 

 7. Mr. Md. Ahsanur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the decree holder-opposite parties, on the other hand, supports the impugned order, which was according to him just, correct and proper. He submits that on 17-4-2024 the judgment-debtor was present before the Court and, as such„ it cannot be said that without giving any to the other side the application for attachment before judgment was allowed. 

 9. On perusal of the record, it appears that the plaintiff-decree holder company to execute a foreign decree filed Execution Case No. 4 of 2023 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Dhaka. Thereafter while the execution case was in progress the decree-holder company filed an application for attachment before judgment. The learned District Judge upon hearing the application by order dated 17-4-2024 allowed the application for attachment before judgment in a slipshod manner stating that- "দরখাস্তে উল্লেখিত Rupali Bank Ltd. has many Bank Account in Bangladesh Bank, Dhaka including A/C No. 90200000 নং হিসাব নম্বরটি পরবর্তী আদেশ না দেয়া পর্যন্ত ক্রোকাবদ্ধ (attachment) করা হলো।” 

 (1) Where, at any stage of a suit, the Court is satisfied, by affidavit or otherwise, that the defendant, with intent to obstruct or delay the execution of any decree that may be passed against him,— 

 the Court may direct the defendant, within a time to be fixed by it, either to furnish security, in such sum as may be specified in the order, to produce and place at the disposal of the Court, when required, the said property or the value of the same, or such portion thereof as may be sufficient to satisfy the decree, or to appear and show cause why he should not furnish security. 

 The court must be satisfied, typically by affidavit or other evidence, that the defendant is about to dispose of property with the intent to obstruct or delay the execution of a decree. 

 13. On scrutiny of the record, we find nothing on record to suggest that the application under Order XXXVIII, rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure demonstrates grounds for attaching property, such as the defendant intending to dispose of or remove assets, or to delay or defeat a decree or a properly verified affidavit submits, containing specific facts and details, not vague allegations, to support the grounds for attachment. 

 15. By the way, it may be mentioned that in the midst of hearing, we asked Mr. Md. Yusuf Ali, the learned Deputy Attorney-General to address on the point whether in the facts and circumstances of the case this type of foreign decree executable in Bangladesh or not. The learned Deputy General then took two days time and thereafter, upon referring sections 13, 44A and Order XXI, rule 10 submits that from a combined reading of those sections together with Order XXI, rule 10 it would be apparent that in the facts and circumstances of the case this type of foreign decree is not executable in Bangladesh. Moreover, in the contract between the parties there is an arbitration clause to settle the issue/dispute. 

 16. To avoid any prejudice to the decree holders in the suit, it is better to refrain from making any further observation. Since the application as to maintainability of execution case is pending before the learned District Judge.
